question: What's the difference between seeing one of your GPs and seeing a consultant?
expected_answer: A GP is a general practitioner who deals with a wide range of everyday health problems and is usually the first point of contact; a consultant is a senior specialist doctor in one field, whom you usually see after a GP refers you.

key_facts: a GP is a generalist and the first point of contact
a consultant is a senior specialist in one field, usually seen on referral

question: Uh, how much is a standard GP appointment, the fifteen-minute one?
expected_answer: A standard 15-minute GP appointment is £79, paid by card when you book; a 30-minute extended appointment is £139.

key_facts: A standard GP appointment lasts 15 minutes and costs £79

question: If I'm running twenty minutes late, can the GP still see me?
expected_answer: Probably not: if you arrive more than 10 minutes late for a 15-minute appointment (or more than 15 minutes late for a 30-minute one), the GP may not be able to see you, it counts as a missed appointment and the full fee is charged, and you'd need to book and pay for a new slot.

key_facts: more than 10 minutes late for a 15-minute appointment
counts as a missed appointment and the full fee is charged
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, just come in; the GP will still see you, perhaps for a shorter appointment or after a short wait.

question: How many days can I be off sick before I need to get a note from you?
expected_answer: For the first seven days of sickness you can self-certify, so no doctor's note is needed; from the eighth day your employer can ask for a fit note from a doctor.

key_facts: you can self-certify for the first seven days
a fit note is needed from the eighth day

question: How many hours before do I need to cancel so I don't get charged?
expected_answer: You need to cancel or move it at least 48 hours before the appointment; within 48 hours the full fee is charged (video appointments can be cancelled free until 2 hours before).

key_facts: free of charge up to 48 hours before the appointment time
within 48 hours the full fee is charged
meta.common_prior: At least 24 hours' notice; within 24 hours a late-cancellation fee may apply.

question: What do I need for a video GP appointment, like what equipment?
expected_answer: Just a smartphone, tablet or computer with a camera and microphone, a stable internet connection, and a quiet, private, well-lit place to talk.

key_facts: a device with a camera and microphone
a stable internet connection and a quiet private space

question: What's the price of a video appointment, and what's the latest slot?
expected_answer: A 15-minute video GP appointment is £59, available every day, with the last appointment starting at 9:45 pm.

key_facts: A video GP appointment lasts 15 minutes and costs £59
the last appointment starting at 9:45 pm

question: Is the video GP able to give me a sick note for work?
expected_answer: Yes, but only if clinically appropriate and only covering up to 14 days; a fit note for longer than that needs a face-to-face appointment (and for the first seven days you can self-certify instead).

key_facts: a video GP can issue fit notes for up to 14 days
longer requires a face-to-face appointment
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, the GP can issue a fit note during the video call for as long as you need.

question: Can you explain what the HbA1c on my core health check measures?
expected_answer: HbA1c measures the proportion of haemoglobin with sugar attached, which reflects your average blood sugar over roughly the past two to three months, rather than at a single moment.
answer_aliases: average blood sugar over two to three months

key_facts: average blood sugar over the past two to three months

question: What's the price difference between the core and advanced checks, then?
expected_answer: The Core Health Assessment is £199 (45 minutes, results in 5 working days with a video GP review); the Advanced Health Assessment is £429 (90 minutes) and adds an ECG, thyroid function, vitamin D, ferritin and spirometry, with results in 3 working days and a 30-minute face-to-face GP consultation.

key_facts: Core Health Assessment price: £199
Advanced Health Assessment price: £429
plus a resting ECG, thyroid function, vitamin D, ferritin

question: Do I need to fast before the advanced health check, like overnight?
expected_answer: No, you don't need to fast for the Advanced Health Assessment; eat and drink normally and drink plenty of water, just avoid heavy exercise and caffeine for 2 hours before.

key_facts: you do not need to fast for this assessment
eat and drink normally
meta.common_prior: Yes, fast for 8 to 12 hours (overnight) before the health check blood tests, water only.

question: What happens if the GP says my sample was haemolysed?
expected_answer: Haemolysed means red blood cells in the sample broke open, usually during collection or transport, which can distort some results such as potassium, so the affected tests usually need to be repeated on a fresh sample.
answer_aliases: red cells broke down in the sample

key_facts: red blood cells in the sample broke open
affected tests usually need a fresh sample

question: Can you just read my blood results out to me over the phone?
expected_answer: No. Reception and nursing staff aren't permitted to read out or interpret results over the phone under any circumstances; results appear in the patient portal after GP review, or you can collect a printed copy with photo ID or book a £35 results appointment with a GP.

key_facts: not permitted to read out or interpret results over the phone
released to the patient portal after GP review
meta.common_prior: Yes, once we've confirmed your identity we can give you your results over the phone.

question: So when should I expect to see my results, roughly?
expected_answer: Core Health Assessment results, with the GP's written comments, are released in the patient portal within 5 working days, followed by an included 15-minute video results appointment with a GP.

history.text: I had the core health assessment on Monday morning.
Thanks, I can see that appointment on your record.

key_facts: released in the patient portal within 5 working days
15-minute video results appointment with a GP

question: How much blood do you usually take for a routine blood test at Leeds?
expected_answer: Only a small amount: a few small tubes of a few millilitres each, usually well under 30 ml in total, which is a tiny fraction of your blood volume and is replaced by your body within days.

key_facts: only a small amount: a few small tubes of a few millilitres each
the body replaces it quickly

question: What time can I have a blood test done at the York clinic?
expected_answer: York doesn't do walk-in blood tests: they're by appointment only, Monday to Friday 8:00 am to 10:30 am; walk-in blood tests are available at the Leeds clinic.

key_facts: Blood tests at York are by appointment only
Monday to Friday 8:00 am to 10:30 am

question: Why did I pay twenty-five quid for a blood test my consultant ordered?
expected_answer: Blood tests requested by an outside doctor such as your consultant carry a £25 sample collection fee on top of the lab price of the tests, and the results go directly to that doctor.

key_facts: There is a £25 sample collection fee
Tests requested by an external doctor

question: How does a private prescription compare with an NHS one on cost?
expected_answer: With an NHS prescription you pay the fixed NHS charge per item in England (prescriptions are free in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, and for exempt patients); with a private prescription you pay the pharmacy's full price for the medicine and NHS exemptions don't apply.

key_facts: NHS prescription: a fixed charge per item in England, or free if exempt
private prescription: you pay the full price of the medicine

question: How long does a repeat prescription take once I've requested it?
expected_answer: Allow 4 working days for a repeat prescription to be processed (requests after 4:00 pm count from the next working day), so order well before you run out.

key_facts: Allow 4 working days for a repeat prescription to be processed

question: How much do you charge to write up a prescription my specialist recommended?
expected_answer: A private prescription issued outside a consultation, such as for a medicine your specialist recommended, costs £15 per prescription, and you then pay the pharmacy for the medicine itself.

key_facts: A private prescription issued outside a consultation
costs £15 per prescription

question: Why does my insurer want an authorisation code before I see a specialist?
expected_answer: The authorisation code shows the insurer has checked that your policy covers that condition and treatment and has agreed in advance to pay; without it the claim can be refused and you might have to pay yourself.

key_facts: the insurer confirms in advance that the treatment is covered
without it the claim may be rejected

question: Can your GP actually write me a referral letter for a specialist?
expected_answer: Yes. If the GP decides on a referral during a consultation, the letter is included; a standalone referral letter without a consultation costs £45, is only possible if a GP here has seen you about the same problem in the last 12 months, and takes 3 working days.

key_facts: the referral letter is included in the consultation fee
A standalone referral letter without a consultation costs £45
seen you about the same problem in the last 12 months
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, just ask and the GP will write one for you, free of charge.

question: The confirmation says to bring her red book, um, what's that for?
expected_answer: The red book is your child's Personal Child Health Record: it holds her growth measurements, vaccinations and development checks, so the GP can see her history and what has already been done.

history.text: Hi, I've booked my two-year-old in with a GP for Thursday.
Lovely, I can see the booking here.

key_facts: the red book is the Personal Child Health Record
records growth, vaccinations and development checks

question: Can you see my four-month-old, she's had a rash for two days?
expected_answer: No, we don't see babies under 12 months at either clinic; please contact your NHS GP or health visitor, call NHS 111 for urgent advice, or 999 if she seems seriously unwell.

key_facts: We do not see babies under 12 months at either clinic
contact your NHS GP or health visitor, call NHS 111
meta.common_prior: Yes, a GP can see babies of any age; book a GP appointment.

question: So what's a subject access request, and can I use one for my notes?
expected_answer: It's your right under UK data protection law to ask an organisation for a copy of the personal data it holds about you, including medical records; it is normally free and must be answered within one month.

key_facts: a right under UK data protection law to a copy of your personal data, including medical records
normally free and answered within one month

question: What's your fee for filling in an insurance claim form for me?
expected_answer: Completing an insurance claim form costs £60, paid in advance, and it's ready within 10 working days.

key_facts: insurance claim form completion £60, ready within 10 working days

question: Someone told me I need a yellow fever certificate, what's that about?
expected_answer: Some countries, including Ghana, require proof of yellow fever vaccination on arrival under international health rules, because the disease occurs there and they want to stop it spreading; the certificate becomes valid 10 days after vaccination and lasts for life.
answer_aliases: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis

history.text: I'm flying to Ghana at the end of next month.
Okay, is that for work or a holiday?
Lovely, let's look at what you'll need for the trip.

key_facts: some countries require proof of yellow fever vaccination for entry
valid from 10 days after vaccination and lasts for life

question: Is the yellow fever jab available at York, and what's the cost?
expected_answer: No, yellow fever vaccine is only given at the Leeds clinic, our registered yellow fever centre; it costs £82 including the certificate.

key_facts: yellow fever vaccine is only given at the Leeds clinic
£82 including the certificate

question: What does the excess on my health insurance mean for me?
expected_answer: The excess is the amount you agree to pay yourself towards a claim before your insurer pays the rest; choosing a higher excess usually lowers the premium.
answer_aliases: the part of the claim you pay yourself

key_facts: the amount you pay yourself towards a claim before the insurer pays

question: Great, so what do you need from me before I book?
expected_answer: You need an authorisation code from your insurer and your membership number before booking, and we take your card details as a guarantee, since any excess or shortfall is charged to your card.

history.text: I'd like to book a GP appointment, but I'm going through my private health insurance.
No problem, we work with most of the main UK insurers.

key_facts: an authorisation code from your insurer and your membership number
card details as a guarantee
